drafted_from: tool:start-a-recipe-run's own row (its words, input schema, sample runs and steps) and what its sample runs answered here; read it before relying on it
start_here: Say to your AI: "When a recipe of mine is started, by a wake I switched on or by a call, put its steps and its input in my own database as one job waiting for my AI, once per firing", with {"row":"workflow:bring-in-a-framework"}. It runs tool:start-a-recipe-run and answers {"job":"ai-job:workflow:bring-in-a-framework:sample","status":"written"}
no_lists_because: It names no list of yours: it takes its input and keeps only its own rows (the tables ai_job, workflow_recipe, workflow_step, arrival_source) in your own database.
instructions: 1. Say to your AI: "When a recipe of mine is started, by a wake I switched on or by a call, put its steps and its input in my own database as one job waiting for my AI, once per firing", and give it row (The recipe's id (workflow:...).).
2. The AI calls run_resource_operation at @tools with method tools:run, tool tool:start-a-recipe-run and its input (the worked example shows one).
3. Read what comes back: Every recipe row runs as this tool (the recipes' row source names it in invoke_with), with the recipe's id in input.row.

4. It reaches only your own database, with the connection string you hold as own-rows-postgres-connection: it inserts into ai_job and reads workflow_recipe, workflow_step and arrival_source, and the table an arrival source names.
